chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Whoever practices fortune-telling or goes to see a fortune-teller has indeed despised the religion of Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). I asked: What about physiognomy? He replied: I do not like you to go to them, and whatever they say is not far from what they say, and he said: Physiognomy is a remnant of Prophethood that has passed among the people.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fortune-telling and physiognomy in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith in *Al-Khisal* to distinguish between the absolute rejection of fortune-telling (*al-takwin*) and the nuanced, albeit discouraged, practice of physiognomy (*al-qaifah*). The Imam characterizes physiognomy as a 'remnant of Prophethood' (*fadla min al-nubuwwa*), suggesting it retains a fragment of intuitive insight but lacks the certainty and authority of true revelation.
